established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) are actively used to translate high-level network intents into low-level configurations and to assist configuration translation across vendors; multiple recent works report feasible intent-to-configuration systems and prototype evaluations.
limitations: Most reported evaluations are prototypes or testbed/simulated datasets rather than broad production deployments.
Performance and safety depend on dataset, model tuning, and verification steps used in each study.

established_findings.statement: Augmenting LLMs with external tools, validators, or task-specific calculators substantially improves correctness and reduces certain classes of errors compared to baseline LLM-only configurations in empirical studies.
established_findings.evidence_type: empirical comparative studies and system evaluations
limitations: Reported improvements are conditional on the domain, tool quality, and how tools are integrated; numerical gains vary by task and dataset.
Evidence is drawn from heterogeneous domains (healthcare, engineering benchmarks, agent runtimes), not solely NetOps.

established_findings.statement: Hallucinations and semantic/functional errors in LLM-generated code or configurations are well-documented problems; surveys and empirical analyses identify taxonomy, causes, and mitigation directions.
limitations: Taxonomies and measurements are broad and may categorize diverse failure modes that differ in operational impact for NetOps-specific tasks.
Mitigations evaluated vary in maturity and generality.

established_findings.statement: Constrained or neurosymbolic decoding and grammar- or semantics-aware generation techniques can enforce syntactic or richer semantic constraints at generation time and have been shown to increase validity of structured outputs in experiments.
limitations: These approaches can trade off flexibility (e.g., increased false refusals) and may require domain grammars or tooling that are nontrivial to construct for complex vendor CLIs.
Reported results are task-dependent and may not guarantee full semantic correctness.

established_findings.statement: At least one large-scale production-focused deployment of multi-agent LLMs for network management (Confucius) has been reported with sustained internal use, illustrating that integrated LLM-agent frameworks can be operationalized in large networks with validator integration.
limitations: The report is an experience/system paper and may not include exhaustive independent evaluation metrics or public datasets for external reproduction.
Operational context (scope of tasks onboarded, human oversight policies) constrains generalization.

unresolved_questions.statement: How reliably do LLM-based intent-to-configuration systems generalize to diverse, real-world vendor configurations and large-scale production networks under adversarial or out-of-distribution inputs?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: gap identified by system papers and reviews
limitations: Existing studies show feasibility but typically evaluate on constrained datasets or testbeds; direct large-scale generalization evidence is limited in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What standardized benchmarks, metrics, and workflow-centred evaluations best capture operational reliability, safety, and rollback-worthiness for agentic NetOps systems?
limitations: Surveys and methodological papers call for workflow-centred evaluation but do not converge on a single standardized benchmark within the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do tool-augmentation and constrained decoding eliminate high-risk silent failures (semantic misconfigurations) versus merely reducing syntactic/low-level errors?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: empirical results and method papers indicating partial mitigation
limitations: Available empirical evidence shows improvements but is heterogeneous; direct measurements of high-stakes semantic failure rates in NetOps are not comprehensively reported in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How large and representative are public datasets of real-world router/switch configurations for reproducible evaluation of LLM-driven NetOps pipelines?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: dataset and evaluation-location concerns raised in applied studies
limitations: The supplied records discuss datasets and evaluations but do not catalog comprehensive public corpora of production device configurations.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a need for reproducible, NetOps-focused generate–validate–repair benchmark suites that pair intent prompts, vendor-specific target configs, deterministic validators, and adversarial/perturbed test cases.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: identified gap from review and evaluation studies
limitations: Several papers call for improved evaluation but do not themselves release a unified benchmark covering all listed elements in the supplied record set.

candidate_gaps.statement: Operational attack surfaces for agentic NetOps (e.g., indirect prompt injection, tool-response timing attacks) are documented in adjacent agent-security work but are under-explored specifically for network-configuration pipelines.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: security analyses and attack demonstrations in agent literature
limitations: Attack studies are in the broader agent/LLM context; concrete exploit demonstrations targeting NetOps pipelines are not prominent in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Evidence is limited on end-to-end human-in-the-loop governance protocols (approval thresholds, canary rollouts, automated rollback) tied to quantitative safety metrics for LLM-driven NetOps actions.
limitations: Framework papers recommend governance layers, but detailed, reproducible protocols and metrics for human approvals and rollback are not fully specified in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Transfer of constrained-decoding and neurosymbolic repair methods from code-generation benchmarks to vendor-specific network CLIs requires domain grammars and tooling that appear to be only partially available or reported.
limitations: Papers demonstrate constrained decoding benefits on structured tasks; explicit artifacts (vendor grammars, CLI parsers) for NetOps translation are not uniformly published in the supplied set.

excluded_claims: LLMs (without validators/tools and governance) are proven safe for fully autonomous, unsupervised production NetOps change execution (no supplied record demonstrates universal production safety without surrounding machinery).
Constrained decoding or neurosymbolic methods guarantee complete semantic correctness for all vendor configurations (supplied method papers report improvements but not absolute guarantees).

Tool-augmentation universally doubles correctness across all NetOps tasks (some empirical studies report large gains in specific domains, but no supplied record establishes a universal multiplicative factor for NetOps).
